title: A Landfall for the Summit
premise: Paloma Voss, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy officially denies exists, has spent years staying off every map and out of every ledger. When an upriver scientific expedition goes silent, he is the only one who knows the water well enough to follow it—and the only one who suspects the wreck he's been diving holds the reason the river's source was closed off decades ago. Dragged into an alliance with expedition survivor Mara Quist, whose brother led the lost team, Paloma must choose between the anonymity that keeps him alive and the justice the drowned deserve. At the forbidden source, they uncover a cover-up that cost lives on both sides of the law, and Paloma trades his invisibility for testimony, finding in Mara a love worth standing in the open for.
about_author: Ansel Whitlock is the pen name of a former maritime surveyor who spent eleven seasons working remote rivers before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people the maps forgot, from a cabin he refuses to geotag.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Paloma dives the unnamed wreck at dawn, cataloging cargo that shouldn't exist—a navy vessel sunk where no navy admits operating. His POV establishes his careful invisibility: cash jobs, no records, a boat registered to a dead man. The emotional beat is wary competence shadowed by old guilt over why he left legitimate work.

chapters.title: Static on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: A supply runner hires Paloma to check on the Meridian expedition, silent for nine days upstream. Radio calls go unanswered; the last transmission mentions 'the source' and cuts mid-word. Paloma declines—until he recognizes the voice of the expedition leader as someone from his past. Beat: dread disguised as reluctance.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma preps his shallow-draft boat, hiding dive gear and a rifle among salvage equipment. Flashbacks reveal he once dove this same river for a recovery contract that ended badly and sealed his retreat from the world. Beat: the past surfacing like a body he thought he'd weighted down.

chapters.title: Mara at the Landing
chapters.summary: At the last inhabited landing, Paloma finds Mara Quist waiting—expedition sister, refused passage by everyone else. She forces her way aboard with a satellite phone full of her brother's final coordinates. Their friction crackles: she needs answers, he needs silence. Beat: two stubborn wills sharing one current.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: Running the first gorge nearly kills them both; Paloma's skill saves the boat, earning Mara's grudging respect. They find the expedition's abandoned cache—food untouched, gear stacked neatly, as if walked away from voluntarily. Beat: unease deepening into genuine fear.

chapters.title: The Burned Camp
chapters.summary: They reach the expedition's second camp, burned deliberately, one tent stake driven through a chart marking the wreck site. Mara realizes whoever did this knew exactly what her brother had found. First sign they're being followed: a boat wake across the far channel. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Men Without Insignia
chapters.summary: Unmarked men question Paloma at a fuel stop, offering money to turn back and threats beneath the courtesy. He lies smoothly but recognizes their type—he used to work alongside it. That night he tells Mara a partial truth about his past. Beat: trust built on incomplete foundations.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Coordinates
chapters.summary: Mara decrypts her brother's backup drive: photos of the wreck's hold, manifests stamped classified, and a note—'they sank it on purpose.' The expedition wasn't science; it was proof-gathering. Beat: the mission transforms from rescue to reckoning.

chapters.title: Night Runners
chapters.summary: Pursuers attack at anchor after dark; Paloma runs the rapids blind by moonlight, taking damage, losing supplies. Mara proves steady under fire, and something unspoken shifts between them in the aftermath. Beat: intimacy forged in adrenaline and shared danger.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: They find Tomas Reyes, expedition engineer, half-dead in a root hollow—sole survivor. His account: the team found live ordnance and documents proving the navy scuttled its own ship to bury evidence of a disaster that killed civilians. Then armed men came. Beat: grief and fury braided together.

chapters.title: Triage on the Water
chapters.summary: With Tomas feverish, Paloma must choose: run for help and lose the trail, or push upstream while Tomas fades. Mara argues for the source; Paloma argues for mercy; Tomas himself votes for the truth. Beat: the theme crystallized—the price of survival measured against the price of silence.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Bells
chapters.summary: A legendary gorge where the river narrows to a roar locals say swallows sound itself. They portage under pursuit, Mara spraining an ankle, Paloma carrying her and the evidence both. A pursuer falls in the gorge; Paloma tries to save him and fails. Beat: compassion that costs.

chapters.title: Confession in the Rain
chapters.summary: Stormbound under a ledge, Paloma finally tells all: years ago he dove the wreck on a secret contract, found the same evidence, took hush money, and buried it—that's what his invisibility was bought with. Mara's response isn't forgiveness yet, but understanding. Beat: love against duty, duty losing ground.

chapters.title: The Navy's Wake
chapters.summary: A patrol boat sweeps the upper river; they hide Tomas in a flooded cave while Paloma baits the patrol away, nearly dying in the process. He returns to find Mara kept the camp alive through the night. Beat: devotion demonstrated rather than declared.

chapters.title: Where the Maps End
chapters.summary: Past the last survey marker, the river turns spring-fed and impossibly clear. Signs of the old closure appear: rusted barriers, warning plaques shot through. Tomas worsens; time is now measured in hours. Beat: awe laced with urgency.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: They reach the source: a vast submerged cavern system feeding the river—and inside it, the wreck's missing sister section, deliberately dynamited shut, containing the full record of the civilian deaths. Her brother's final camp sits above it, journals intact. Beat: revelation as devastation.

chapters.title: What Daniel Found
chapters.summary: Reading her brother's journals, Mara learns he'd contacted Paloma's old handler, hoping to flip him—an alliance Paloma never knew was offered. The ambush that killed the team was meant to look like nature. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose; the dead demand witnesses.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Headwaters
chapters.summary: The pursuers arrive in force to erase the site and everyone in it. Paloma collapses the cavern entrance with dive charges—not to hide the truth but to force the navy to excavate publicly, since a sealed site can't be quietly cleaned. Climax begins: violence, sacrifice, Tomas holding the line wounded. Beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Climax: Paloma surfaces the evidence buoy into open water where a news helicopter—Mara's doing, a beacon she'd rigged days earlier—catches it all on camera. The commander orders fire, then stands down as the story goes live. Men without insignia become men with names. Beat: justice arriving not by law but by exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Aftermath at the landing: inquiries announced, careers ending, Tomas hospitalized and talking. Paloma gives a sworn statement under his real name for the first time in years, surrendering his invisibility willingly. Some officers circle wagons; the tide has turned regardless. Beat: the price paid, counted and accepted.

chapters.title: The Weight Above Water
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Paloma dives the wreck one last time—now a protected site, divers welcome, names read aloud at the surface. He retrieves nothing; everything needed has already come up. Mara waits on the boat. Beat: peace earned, not granted.

chapters.title: A Landfall for the Summit
chapters.summary: Epilogue: Paloma and Mara launch upriver together, not fleeing this time but mapping openly, Tomas recovered at the helm. The wilderness still forgives nothing—but they've stopped asking it to forget. Final beat: love chosen freely, duty redefined as witness, the summit reached by coming home.
